config.prompt: From the first others to the edited self — order the construction line:
items: The play stage — taking the attitude of significant others
The game stage — the generalised other, society's standpoint internalised
The 'I' and the 'me' form a dialogue
Cooley's looking-glass self — imagine their judgment, and adjust
Habitus — durable dispositions acquired through practical experience of a class position
Goffman's front stage and back stage — the self continuously edited for its audience
config.why: Each layer installs inside the last: roles first, the internalised standpoint next, then the embodied dispositions and the performance that edits them for every audience.

activities.caption: pair each Marxian term with what it names
activities.name: stmMarxMatch

config.prompt: Pair each term with what it names:

pairs.right: social relations between people appear as relations between things — prices seem like properties of objects
the variable the whole theory turns on — a class 'in itself' becomes 'for itself' only through struggle
four faces in the 1844 Manuscripts — from the product, the activity, other workers, your species-capacities
workers sharing a platform, algorithmically supervised, individually isolated — the mechanism under live observation

config.why: The system is invisible from inside because relations between people present themselves as relations between things — which is what makes the consciousness variable so hard to switch on.

config.root: A family with money wants its child to carry 'natural' fluency. Bourdieu's conversion circuit:

start.text: Step one: money becomes instruments, ease and embodied fluency. What just happened?

choices.label: Economic capital converted into cultural capital
Cultural capital converted into economic capital

wrong1.text: Not yet — the money came first; the purchase builds the fluency, not the reverse.

choices.label: Run it the right way round

conv2.text: Step two: where does that fluency convert back into money?

choices.label: At the gates where fluency reads as merit

wrong2.text: That is spending, not conversion — the payoff comes where fluency is judged.

conv3.text: Step three: what does the circuit do to the appearance of meritocracy?

choices.label: Its measurement instruments partly measure inherited advantage
It proves outcomes track pure talent

end2.text: That is the comfortable reading — the lesson's uncomfortable summary corrects it: the instruments partly measure inherited advantage.

end.text: Meritocracy's measurement instruments partly measure inherited advantage — reproduction without an explicit handshake.

config.why: Economic to cultural at the purchases; cultural to economic at the gates where fluency reads as merit; habitus does the carrying between them.

activities.anchor: Personality is individual and varies within classes
activities.caption: true or false — the habitus label
activities.name: stmHabitusJudge

statements.s: Habitus is acquired through explicit teaching.
statements.why: It is absorbed through practical experience of a class position, operating without explicit teaching.

statements.s: People from the same background feel 'at home' in some institutions and 'not for the likes of us' in others without ever being told.
statements.why: That silent comfort map is the habitus doing its work.

statements.s: Inequality reproduces itself silently through comfort and discomfort.
Habitus is the same thing as temperament.
statements.why: Temperament belongs to the person; habitus is class-shared — the two can disagree.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — the control mechanisms
activities.name: stmControlSpot

config.prompt: One line of this summary is wrong — click it:
lines: Durkheim: control fails when regulation collapses — anomie, the normless state of sudden change.
Weber: we obey because authority is believed — traditional, charismatic, or rational-legal.
Foucault: the panopticon works through visible but unverifiable watching, so the watcher moves inside.
Marx: the ruling ideas of each age are the ideas of its ruling class.
The three mechanisms are rivals: exactly one of norms, legitimacy and internalised surveillance is true.
config.correction: They are not rivals — norms, legitimacy and internalised surveillance interlock: three mechanisms, not one.
config.why: Durkheim's norms, Weber's legitimacy and Foucault's internalised surveillance do most of the daily work together, with informal sanction behind them.

activities.anchor: Most social control never involves the state
activities.caption: drag between the machine's two halves
activities.name: stmInformalCompare

config.prompt: Drag between the machine's two halves:

before.label: Informal
before.text: shame, gossip, exclusion, side-eye — ridicule policing would-be big men, ostracism as the supreme penalty; today the workplace peer-review, the group chat, the school corridor: reputational systems with real teeth.

after.label: Formal
after.text: police, courts, examination systems — the visible fraction of a much larger machine; law works because informal sanction backs it, and informal norms harden into law when they matter enough.

config.why: When watching is continuous and unverifiable, it moves inside — and the guard towers become unnecessary.

activities.caption: bet before you read on — the composite case
activities.name: stmIntersectPredict

config.q: A 1976 US lawsuit alleged a harm that was neither the racism Black men could claim nor the sexism white women could claim. What did the court do?
choices: Recognised the composite category for the first time
Ruled against the plaintiffs — the claims fit race or sex singly, and the composite fit neither template
Dismissed on procedural grounds — the filings were late
Ordered the company to change its layoff system
config.why: Crenshaw (1989) built intersectionality on the case: the disadvantage is non-additive — an intersection the law's separate categories could not represent at all.

activities.caption: pair each instrument with what it reads
activities.name: stmCapitalMatch

config.prompt: Pair each instrument with what it reads:

pairs.right: the group people measure themselves against before they belong to it — aspiration as a social fact
the student dressing like the profession she means to enter
in-group solidarity — the kind that comforts
ties across groups — the kind that gets you jobs
who you can call, who vouches for you, whose tables you can be seen at

config.why: Putnam's Bowling Alone (2000) made the aggregate case measurable — and the two capitals trade off: the policies that build one are not those that build the other.
